title: Dataverse security roles: who can read or change which data?
summary: The page passes: Microsoft documentation supports the role model, licensing qualifications, controls and audit events. Minor corrections would complete the application-user navigation path and add the linked licensing overview to the source list.

claims.claim: Role privileges are reached in Power Platform admin center through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + Permissions > Security roles > security role.
claims.quote: Select Users + Permissions > Security roles.

claims.claim: POST [Organization Uri]/api/data/v9.2/roles(<role-id>)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.AddPrivilegesRole adds privileges to the role.
claims.quote: POST [Organization Uri]/api/data/v9.2/roles(44ee44ee-ff55-aa66-bb77-88cc88cc88cc)/Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.AddPrivilegesRole HTTP/1.1

claims.claim: Direct user role assignments are managed through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles.
claims.quote: Select Users + permissions, and then select Users. On the Users page select a user, and then select Manage security roles.

claims.claim: POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.0/systemusers(azureactivedirectoryobjectid=<user object ID>)/systemuserroles_association/$ref assigns a role using the role's @odata.id.

The application-user role selection path runs through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users > + New app user > Create a new app user > edit icon (security roles).
claims.quote: Select + Add an app to choose the registered Microsoft Entra application that was created for the selected user, and then select Add.
claims.fix: Use the fuller path 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users > + New app user > Create a new app user > + Add an app > application > Add > Business Unit > business unit > edit icon (security roles)' in the front matter and rendered row. The omitted application and business-unit target selections are not a blocker.

claims.claim: pac admin assign-user --environment <environment-id> --user <application-id> --role <role> --application-user assigns an application user the specified security role.
claims.quote: Object ID or user principal name (UPN) of Microsoft Entra ID user to be assigned to the environment or Application ID if assigning an Application User.

claims.claim: License-to-role mappings can be viewed through Environments > environment > Settings > Users + Permissions > License To Role mapping.
claims.quote: Go to Environments > [select an environment] > Settings > Users + Permissions > License To Role mapping.

claims.claim: No API or command for Dataverse License To Role mapping was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse "License To Role mapping" API PowerShell CLI; "license" "role mapping" Dataverse API; Dataverse license role mapping Web API; "License To Role" PowerShell. Read assign-security-roles, pac admin and Role entity reference; no mapping operation found.

claims.claim: Record ownership across business units is enabled through Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Record ownership across business units.
claims.quote: Select Settings > Product > Features. Turn on Record ownership across business units.

claims.claim: Microsoft.Crm.SE.OrgDBOrgSettingsTool.exe Update /u <organization-unique-name> EnableOwnershipAcrossBusinessUnits <value> changes the ownership-across-business-units setting.
claims.quote: To update Microsoft.Crm.SE.OrgDBOrgSettingsTool.exe Update [/u] <OrgName> <SettingName> <Value>

claims.claim: Security Role auditing is enabled through Environments > environment > Settings > Audit and logs > Entity and field audit settings > Entities > Security Role > General > Data Services > Auditing.
claims.quote: In the left side panel, under Entities, select Security Role. On the General tab, under Data Services, select Auditing.

claims.claim: PUT [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/EntityDefinitions(LogicalName='role') updates the Security Role table definition, including its auditing setting.
claims.quote: PUT [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/EntityDefinitions(LogicalName='new_bankaccount') HTTP/1.1

claims.quote:

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risks and limits: Predefined roles
claims.claim: The predefined-role reference says its listed Dataverse roles cannot be edited.
claims.quote: The following list provides the predefined security roles in an environment that has a Dataverse database. You can't edit these roles.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risks and limits: Predefined roles
claims.claim: The editing guide documents editing role privileges but excludes System Administrator.
claims.quote: You can't edit the System Administrator security role. Instead, copy the System Administrator security role and make changes to the new role.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: Who can change roles
claims.claim: Assigning Dataverse roles needs System Administrator or a custom role with at least Read and Assign on the Security Role table.
claims.quote: System Administrator security role, or a custom Dataverse role with at least Read and Assign privileges on the Security Role table

claims.claim: The role overview's troubleshooting table instead lists only System Administrator or a tenant-level admin role for managing assignments.
claims.quote: Only users with the System Administrator role or a tenant-level admin role can manage security role assignments.

claims.claim: An environment can have only one application user for each Microsoft Entra app registration.
claims.quote: In an environment, you can only have one application user for each Microsoft Entra-registered application.

claims.claim: Application-user creation involves choosing the application and business unit before using the security-role edit icon.
claims.quote: Under Business Unit, select a business unit from the dropdown list.

claims.claim: License-based default role management does not apply in Dataverse for Teams, Trial or Developer environments.
claims.quote: License-based default role management isn't applicable for users in these types of environments: Dataverse for Teams, Trial, and Developer.

claims.claim: Enabling Record ownership across business units requires a Dynamics 365 admin or Power Platform admin.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Power Platform admin center as a Dynamics 365 admin or Microsoft Power Platform admin.

claims.claim: EnableOwnershipAcrossBusinessUnits stores the feature state and can be changed with OrgDBOrgSettings.
claims.quote: The EnableOwnershipAcrossBusinessUnits setting stores the state of this feature. You can also change the setting with the OrgDBOrgSettings tool for Microsoft Dynamics CRM.

claims.where: controls[5].note; Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Environment auditing must be enabled before Security Role auditing records changes.
claims.quote:
Prerequisites

Turn on auditing in your environment.

claims.claim: IsAuditEnabled.Value controls whether the table is enabled for auditing.
claims.quote: Tables and columns each have a managed property named IsAuditEnabled that controls whether they're enabled for auditing.

claims.claim: The PUT update should preserve the other properties in the retrieved table definition.
claims.quote: Therefore, you must use the PUT method when updating data model entities and be careful to include all the existing properties that you don't intend to change. You can't update individual properties.

claims.claim: Publish the table customizations for the metadata change to take effect.
claims.quote: When you update a table or column definition, use the PublishXml Action before the changes you make are applied to the model-driven applications.

claims.claim: A Dataverse security role is a set of privileges governing access to tables and records for users, teams or application users in one environment.
claims.quote: Dataverse security roles | System Administrator, System Customizer, Basic User | Single environment (with Dataverse) | Control access to Dataverse tables, apps, and data within an environment that has a Dataverse database.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents the Dataverse security model as applying only to environments with a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: The model applies only to environments that have a Dataverse database.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: Table privileges include Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append, Append to, Assign and Share.
claims.quote: Table privileges define which tasks a user with access to a table record can do, such as Read, Create, Delete, Write, Assign, Share, Append, and Append To.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: Miscellaneous task privileges are another of the three role privilege types.
claims.quote: Miscellaneous privileges: These task-based privileges give a user permission to perform specific, miscellaneous (nonrecord) tasks, such as publish articles or activate business rules.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: Privacy-related privileges are a third type and include exporting data to Excel.
claims.quote: Privacy-related privileges: These privileges give a user permission to perform tasks that involve data that's integrated, downloaded, or exported outside of Dataverse, such as exporting data to Microsoft Excel or printing.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: An access level determines how deep in the business unit hierarchy a privilege applies.
claims.quote: Access levels determine how deep in the business unit hierarchy the user can perform the privilege.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: The access levels are Organization, Parent: Child Business Unit, Business Unit, User and None.
claims.quote: Parent: Child Business Unit | Users can access records in their business unit and all business units subordinate to it.

claims.where: What it is: How a role is built
claims.claim: Organization-owned tables, miscellaneous privileges and privacy-related privileges have only Organization or None access levels.
claims.quote: For organization-owned tables, miscellaneous privileges and privacy-related privileges only have access levels of Organization or None.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Security roles can be assigned directly to users or to Dataverse teams.
claims.quote: Assign security roles directly to users or to Dataverse teams.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Team members receive privileges assigned to the team.
claims.quote: Team members receive the privileges assigned to the team.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters; Risks and limits: Cumulative access
claims.claim: Users can hold multiple roles; role and team privileges are cumulative, so a narrower role cannot hide records granted by a broader role.
claims.quote: Security privileges are cumulative. A user receives the broadest access granted by all their roles and team memberships.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Business units define security boundaries.
claims.quote: They define security boundaries that help you manage users and data.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Security roles are associated with business units.
claims.quote: Security roles are associated with business units.

claims.where: What it is: How a role reaches a person
claims.claim: Every user belongs to one business unit.
claims.quote: Assign each user to one business unit and assign the user a security role from that business unit.

claims.where: What it is: Roles that are not Dataverse roles
claims.claim: Tenant-level admin roles such as Power Platform administrator are assigned in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Tenant-level admin roles such as Power Platform administrator and Dynamics 365 administrator are assigned in the Microsoft 365 admin center and grant administrative access across environments.

claims.where: What it is: Roles that are not Dataverse roles
claims.claim: Tenant-level admin roles do not by themselves grant Dataverse data access.
claims.quote: However, these roles don't automatically grant Dataverse data access.

claims.where: What it is: Roles that are not Dataverse roles
claims.claim: Environments without a Dataverse database use Environment Admin and Environment Maker as their only predefined roles.
claims.quote: Environment Maker and Environment Admin are the only predefined roles for environments that have no Dataverse database.

claims.claim: Dataverse offers record sharing for exceptions beyond the ownership and business unit model.
claims.quote: Share individual records with a user or team to handle exceptions that your ownership and business unit model doesn't cover.

claims.claim: Column-level security is configured separately from security roles.
claims.quote: Enable column-level security separately for each column. Then create a column security profile that grants Create, Update, and Read access to secured columns.

claims.where: What it is; Risks and limits: Filtered record ownership; Open questions
claims.claim: Filtered record ownership is in preview, and Microsoft says preview features are not meant for production use.
claims.quote:
Filtered table record ownership (preview)

Preview features aren't meant for production use and may have restricted functionality.

claims.claim: Filtered record ownership controls record access using column-value filters.
claims.quote: Filtered record ownership lets admins control access to Dataverse records with column-value filters.

claims.where: Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: The Default environment automatically assigns Basic User to all users added in Dataverse.
claims.quote: For the Default environment type, Basic User and Environment Maker roles are assigned automatically to all users added in Dataverse.

claims.where: Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: The Default environment automatically assigns Environment Maker to all users added in Dataverse.
claims.quote: For the Default environment type, Basic User and Environment Maker roles are assigned automatically to all users added in Dataverse.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends assigning Environment Maker to Copilot Studio authors.
claims.quote: Assign the Environment Maker role to users who need to author agents.

claims.claim: Microsoft allows another predefined or custom role for Copilot Studio authors needing different permissions.
claims.quote: If the user needs a different set of permissions, assign another predefined role or a custom role.

claims.claim: Microsoft Entra tenant admins no longer receive Dataverse System Administrator automatically.
claims.quote: Previously, Microsoft Entra ID admins, including Power Platform admins and Dynamics 365 service admins, were automatically assigned the System Administrator role in Dataverse. This is no longer the case.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Tenant admin
claims.claim: Previously assigned System Administrator roles persist unless removed, including after removal of the tenant admin role.
claims.quote: However, if an admin was previously assigned a role in Dataverse, removing them from the Power Platform admin and Dynamics 365 service admin roles will not automatically remove their System Administrator role in Dataverse.

claims.claim: Microsoft's security role documentation publishes no separate security-role price, license or meter.
claims.quote: Searched: Dataverse security roles separate price license meter charges. Read security-roles-privileges, database-security, assign-security-roles, wp-security-cds and pricing-billing-skus. Product licensing and audit storage are documented; no separate charge for security roles was found.

claims.claim: A user's presence in an environment does not grant Dataverse data access.
claims.quote: A user's presence in an environment doesn't grant access to Dataverse data.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/pricing-billing-skus to the front-matter sources as 'Licensing overview for Microsoft Power Platform'. It is already linked in the body and supports the licensing qualifications.

claims.claim: Users need any required product license in addition to an appropriate security role.
claims.quote: The user must still have an appropriate security role and any required product license.

claims.claim: Dataverse tracks access separately for each database.
claims.quote: Dataverse tracks access separately for each database, and the user must have an appropriate Dataverse license.

claims.claim: Dataverse expects an appropriate Dataverse license for the user's access.
claims.quote: Dataverse tracks access separately for each database, and the user must have an appropriate Dataverse license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Where license-to-role mappings exist, valid licensed users receive the mapped roles automatically.
claims.quote: Users, with a valid license, get corresponding mapped roles assigned to them automatically.

claims.claim: Removing the corresponding license automatically removes its mapped role.
claims.quote: Removal of the respective license results in automatic role removal.

claims.claim: An application user can be created without a license.
claims.quote: You can create an unlicensed application user in your environment.

claims.claim: Dataverse audit logs consume log storage capacity.
claims.quote: Dataverse stores audit logs and they consume log storage capacity.

claims.claim: A Power Platform administrator needs System Administrator in the specific Dataverse environment to work with data.
claims.quote: To work with data in a Dataverse environment, a tenant admin must also be assigned the System Administrator Dataverse security role in that specific environment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Everyone needs a role
claims.claim: Users must have at least one role directly or through a group team; the service denies access without one.
claims.quote: You must assign at least one security role to every user either directly or indirectly as a member of a group team. The service doesn't allow access to users who don't have at least one security role.

claims.claim: An assigner cannot assign a role with more privileges than the assigner holds.
claims.quote: To prevent elevation of security role privileges, the person who is assigning the security role can't assign someone else to a security role that has more privileges than the assigner.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends a custom security role when allowing non-System Administrators to assign roles.
claims.quote: If you have a need to allow non-System Administrators to assign security roles, you should consider creating a custom security role with all the privileges listed in Create an administrative user and prevent elevation of security role privilege.

claims.claim: Some predefined security roles cannot be copied; Microsoft suggests creating a custom role instead.
claims.quote: Some predefined roles can't be copied. Try creating a custom security role instead.

claims.claim: Where copying is supported, an existing role can be copied and privileges set on the new role.
claims.quote: Go back to the Security roles page and select the new role you created. Specify privileges for the security role.

claims.claim: Custom security roles are not supported for canvas apps.
claims.quote: It's important to note that custom security roles are not supported for canvas apps.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Organization-level access; What to check
claims.claim: Organization access reaches records across all business units.
claims.quote: Users can access all records in the organization, regardless of the business unit hierarchical level they or the environment belong to.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Sharing is the exception
claims.claim: Microsoft advises sharing only for exceptions because it is less efficient and harder to troubleshoot than role-based access.
claims.quote: Use sharing only for exceptions because it performs less efficiently and can be harder to troubleshoot than role-based access.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Roles do not unlock columns
claims.claim: Column-level security requires the user already to have record access.
claims.quote: Column-level security doesn't grant access to a record. A user must already have record access before a column security profile can grant access to secured columns.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Roles do not unlock columns
claims.claim: Secured-column access is granted using a column security profile assigned to users or teams.
claims.quote: Then create a column security profile that grants Create, Update, and Read access to secured columns. Assign the profile to users or teams.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Moving between environments
claims.claim: Dataverse solutions can move security roles between environments.
claims.quote: Use Dataverse solutions to move security roles and column security profiles between environments.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Moving between environments
claims.claim: Business units and teams must be created and managed separately in each environment.
claims.quote: Create and manage business units and teams separately in each environment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Moving between environments
claims.claim: User assignments to security components must be made in each environment.
claims.quote: You must also assign users to the appropriate security components in each environment.

claims.where: Risks and limits: PowerShell gap; Open questions
claims.claim: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentRoleAssignment applies to environments without Dataverse and returns 403 Forbidden for an environment with a Dataverse database.
claims.quote: Sets permissions to an environment without a Dataverse database. If you make this call to an environment with a Dataverse database instance, you receive a 403 Forbidden error.

claims.where: Governance controls: Who can change roles
claims.claim: Power Platform, Dynamics 365 and Global Administrators must self-elevate before assigning Dataverse roles.
claims.quote: Power Platform, Dynamics 365, and Global Administrators are no longer automatically assigned the Dataverse System Administrator role. They must self-elevate before assigning Dataverse roles.

claims.where: Governance controls: Who can change roles
claims.claim: A Dynamics 365 Administrator must belong to the environment's security group.
claims.quote: A Dynamics 365 Administrator must belong to the environment's security group. This restriction doesn't apply to Global Administrators or Power Platform Administrators.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Business units constrain available role assignments unless Record ownership across business units allows roles from other units.
claims.quote: When the allow record ownership across business units is enabled, you can assign security roles from different business units to your users irrespective of which business unit the users belong to.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: The role audit report is under Power Platform admin center > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles > Audit report.
claims.quote: Select Environments > [select an environment] > Settings > Users + permissions > Security roles. Select Audit report in the command bar.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Audit event 53 records assigning a role to a team.
claims.quote: 53 | Assign Role To Team | Associate | A security role is assigned to a team.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Audit event 54 records removing a role from a team.
claims.quote: 54 | Remove Role From Team | Disassociate | A security role is removed from a team.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Audit event 55 records assigning a role to a user.
claims.quote: 55 | Assign Role To User | Associate | A security role is assigned to a user.

claims.where: Governance controls: How the controls interact
claims.claim: Audit event 56 records removing a role from a user.
claims.quote: 56 | Remove Role From User | Disassociate | A security role is removed from a user.

claims.where: Governance controls: What the controls do not enforce
claims.claim: Data policies let administrators control connector access.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin center data policies allow administrators to control access to these connectors in various ways to help reduce risk in your organization.
